items.title: Rick Margitza interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 22, 2024
items.q: it wasn’t a full blown article about Jerry Bergonzi — he said sometimes he’ll just go and sit down or lay down on the couch and practice in his head for an hour.

ctx.x: Do you ever get an idea in your head, either from the piano or sax, and then go for a walk and find that you’re working out possibilities in your head?

Yes. Actually I have —I shouldn’t say developed the ability over the years, it’s just something that has happened is, even without, even like aside from composing is that I will practice in my head. There was recently an interesting little — I think it was one of those things called profiles in DownBeat where it wasn’t a full blown article about Jerry Bergonzi — he said sometimes he’ll just go and sit down or lay down on the couch and practice in his head for an hour. And so I’ve kind of — you know when you’re…

and going through all the keys or a certain song and practicing it in different keys in my head, and just kind of imagining the sound and trying to feel the vibrations. And it actually is something that I’ve actually — I work with my students on doing. So I think that’s actually a very beneficial thing to do. And then to answer your first question yes, I do sometimes will go for a walk and work through something that might be part of a song, not a whole song. And then come back and try to get it down on paper and…
